citation: Asr, F.T., Mazraeh, M., Lopes, A., Gautam, V., Gonzales, J., Rao, P., Taboada, M. The Gender Gap Tracker: Using Natural Language Processing to measure gender bias in media
dataset: Seven Canadian English-language online news outlets
method: NER, coreference, quote extraction, name-based gender services
main_result: Men quoted about three times as often as women; pattern stable across outlets and time
limitations: Short window; relies on name-to-gender inference; modern online news only
relation_to_this_project: Closest methodological template for quote counting. We avoid name-based gender inference and study a 64-year span

citation: Jia, S., Lansdall-Welfare, T., Sudhahar, S., Carter, C., Cristianini, N. Women Are Seen More than Heard in Online Newspapers
dataset: Online news articles and images (URLs on Dryad)
measurement: Gender of people mentioned vs. quoted vs. pictured
main_result: Women less often quoted than mentioned or pictured
limitations: Modern online news; name- and pronoun-based classifiers
relation_to_this_project: Source of H7 (quoted share below mentioned share); we test the same contrast historically

citation: Garg, N., Schiebinger, L., Jurafsky, D., Zou, J. Word embeddings quantify 100 years of gender and ethnic stereotypes
dataset: Google Books / COHA embeddings, NYT, U.S. Census
measurement: Embedding association between gender words and occupation/adjective words
method: Diachronic word embeddings compared with Census occupation data
main_result: Embedding bias tracks occupational participation and social movements
limitations: Aggregate association, not person-level representation; embedding instability
relation_to_this_project: Motivates diachronic role associations; our unit is the person-in-article and we compare against direct measurements

citation: Underwood, T., Bamman, D., Lee, S. The Transformation of Gender in English-Language Fiction
method: BookNLP character extraction with pronoun-based gender; predictive models
main_result: Gendered description of characters becomes less differentiated over time; share of fiction written by women falls 1850-1950
limitations: Fiction rather than news; pronoun-based gender inference
relation_to_this_project: Closest historical analogue; pronoun-based character gender parallels our tier 2

citation: Dell, M., Carlson, J., Bryan, T., Silcock, E., Arora, A., Shen, Z., D'Amico-Wong, L., Le, Q., Querubin, P., Heldring, L. American Stories: A Large-Scale Structured Text Dataset of Historical U.S. Newspapers
dataset: Chronicling America scans re-processed with layout detection and OCR
main_result: Tens of millions of structured historical articles released CC-BY-4.0
limitations: OCR noise; uneven digitisation across papers and years
relation_to_this_project: Our corpus. Its coverage cliff at 1923 and per-paper imbalance are modelled explicitly

citation: van Strien, D., Beelen, K., Ardanuy, M.C., Hosseini, K., McGillivray, B., Colavizza, G. Assessing the Impact of OCR Quality on Downstream NLP Tasks
measurement: Effect of OCR errors on sentence segmentation, NER, dependency parsing, IR, topic models, LM fine-tuning
method: Controlled comparison of OCR vs. corrected text
main_result: OCR noise harms downstream tasks, with effects that vary widely by task
relation_to_this_project: Justifies OCR-quality stratification and the legible-only robustness spec

citation: Devinney, H., Björklund, J., Björklund, H. Theories of "Gender" in NLP Bias Research
measurement: How papers define and operationalise gender
main_result: Most papers leave their theory of gender implicit, few are inclusive of non-binary genders, and many conflate sex, social gender and linguistic gender
relation_to_this_project: Motivates explicit separation of textual gender signal from identity in our measurement framework

citation: Hamilton, W.L., Leskovec, J., Jurafsky, D. Diachronic Word Embeddings Reveal Statistical Laws of Semantic Change
dataset: Six historical corpora in four languages
main_result: Frequent words change more slowly; polysemous words change faster
relation_to_this_project: Warns that role terms (e.g. 'secretary') drift in meaning; motivates context-based role methods over fixed lexicons

citation: Antoniak, M., Mimno, D. Evaluating the Stability of Embedding-based Word Similarities
main_result: Nearest-neighbour similarities are highly sensitive to corpus composition, especially in small corpora
relation_to_this_project: Reason we treat embedding neighbourhood analyses as exploratory and bootstrap them

citation: Sap, M., Prasettio, M.C., Holtzman, A., Rashkin, H., Choi, Y. Connotation Frames of Power and Agency in Modern Films
measurement: Power and agency implied by verbs attached to characters
method: Crowdsourced verb connotation lexicon plus dependency parsing
main_result: Female characters portrayed with less power and agency
limitations: Modern film dialogue; lexicon crowdsourced from modern annotators
relation_to_this_project: Informs agent/patient verb analysis; we use syntactic role rather than modern connotation judgements

citation: Fu, L., Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil, C., Lee, L. Tie-breaker: Using language models to quantify gender bias in sports journalism
venue_year: IJCAI Workshop on NLP Meets Journalism (2016)
measurement: Topical focus of journalists' questions by player gender
main_result: Female players asked more questions unrelated to the game
relation_to_this_project: Example of within-topic (sports) comparison; supports topic-conditional analysis

citation: Rudinger, R., Naradowsky, J., Leonard, B., Van Durme, B. Gender Bias in Coreference Resolution
measurement: Occupation-dependent gender bias in coreference systems
main_result: Coreference systems resolve pronouns in occupation-stereotyped ways
relation_to_this_project: Why we avoid learned coreference for gender assignment and use a transparent, validated pronoun rule

citation: Lappin, S., Leass, H.J. An Algorithm for Pronominal Anaphora Resolution
main_result: Salience from syntactic role (subject preference) resolves most pronouns
relation_to_this_project: Basis of our subject-preference salience filter for the pronoun tier

citation: Monroe, B.L., Colaresi, M.P., Quinn, K.M. Fightin' Words: Lexical Feature Selection and Evaluation for Identifying the Content of Political Conflict
method: Log-odds ratio with informative Dirichlet prior
main_result: Regularised log-odds outperforms raw frequency and chi-square for distinctive-word selection
limitations: Group comparison only; no confound control on its own
relation_to_this_project: Our estimator for verb/modifier contrasts (applied within topic strata)

citation: Steegen, S., Tuerlinckx, F., Gelman, A., Vanpaemel, W. Increasing Transparency Through a Multiverse Analysis
measurement: Sensitivity of conclusions to data-processing choices
method: Multiverse analysis across all reasonable processing paths
main_result: Single-path analyses can be misleading; report the full multiverse

citation: World Association for Christian Communication (WACC). Who Makes the News? 6th Global Media Monitoring Project (GMMP 2020)
dataset: News monitored on one day across 116 countries (print, broadcast, digital)
measurement: Share of news subjects and sources who are women
method: Manual coding by trained volunteer monitors
main_result: Women were 25% of people heard or seen in the news in 2020
limitations: Single-day snapshots; manual coding; modern era only
relation_to_this_project: Modern benchmark that our historical series ends well before; used for context only
